clue.text: Hurried to get hold of bill (not in huddle)

indicators.note: to get hold of means one word grips the other, so the bill goes inside the hurried word

parts.note: hurried means sped
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to grab the bill while staying out of a team huddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed definition describes people standing apart rather than bunched together; 'to get hold of' is the container signal, not part of the hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Players set apart at intervals are separated, so they are not bunched up in a huddle.

clue.text: Dress fussily in skirt that's very soft on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the very soft letters sit around the skirt word

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
a rim skirts, or borders, something

explanation.surface: Someone dresses fussily in a skirt that is very soft on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like clothing in this dressing scene, but here it means to border, as an edge does; 'on the outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom oneself with excessive care over one's appearance is to dress fussily.

clue.text: Spanish gent about to join dance — 'erculean fellow

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
a ball is a formal dance
a Herculean fellow is a hero; with the apostrophe dropping the H, as a Cockney would, it becomes ero

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman joins a dance, a Herculean figure with the H dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'erculean marks a dropped H, so HERO loses its H too, leaving ERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A caballero is a Spanish gentleman or horseman, the Spanish equivalent of a cavalier.

clue.text: Us diplomat most boring, unable to reach conclusion

indicators.note: unable to reach conclusion means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: most boring means dullest

explanation.surface: An American diplomat is the dullest of all and can never finish a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unable to reach conclusion' drops the last letter T of DULLEST. John Foster Dulles was US Secretary of State in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: John Foster Dulles served as American Secretary of State under Eisenhower.

clue.text: Wise man hugging me on the street in term-time

indicators.note: hugging means the wise man wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a seer is a wise prophet
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A sage embraces the speaker out on the street during the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' is the container signal, and the definition 'term-time' is read as one word for an academic period.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year academic term, the stretch when teaching happens.

clue.text: No nerdy comrades will be able to mix in school

indicators.note: to mix means the letters of these three words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Unfashionable comrades would fit in well at this kind of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mix' rearranges NO NERDY COMRADES. A secondary modern was a British state school for pupils who did not pass the eleven-plus exam for grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary modern is a kind of British state secondary education establishment.

clue.text: Abuse — awful matter involving a learner

indicators.note: involving means the shuffled word wraps round the other letters
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of matter are jumbled

parts.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A dreadful affair includes a learner being mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns MATTER into MTREAT, and 'involving' puts A and L inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat or ill-use someone is to abuse them.

clue.text: Girl's churning over — it's the laxative

indicators.note: churning over means the girl's name and its s are turned round

parts.note: Anne's is a girl's possessive

explanation.surface: A girl's stomach is churning after taking a laxative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning over' reads ANNES backwards. 'Churning' suggests an upset stomach, apt for a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant-derived purgative used to relieve constipation.

clue.text: I get homes sorted out for four couples maybe

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters of these words are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone arranges housing for four couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges I GET HOMES. An eightsome reel is a Scottish dance for four couples, so the definition is by example, as 'maybe' admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight dancers, as in the Scottish reel, is made up of four pairs.

clue.text: Forging alibi with ' a cold' — wicked!

indicators.note: forging means fabricating, so the letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Faking an alibi of having a cold is a dreadful thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forging' rearranges ALIBI, A and COLD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolical means devilish, extremely evil or cruel.

clue.text: Close in almost complete darkness

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by one letter

parts.note: night is the time of complete darkness

explanation.surface: Something is near at hand in almost total darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter T from NIGHT. 'Close' is the adjective meaning near, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near in place or time.

clue.text: Rascal observed going round china with penny

indicators.note: going round means the observed word encircles the rest

parts.note: observed means seen
china means pal, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate for mate

explanation.surface: A scoundrel was spotted wandering around with a mate and a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the container signal. Spalpeen is an Irish word for a rascal, and china for mate is London rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Spalpeen is an Irish term for a scamp or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Rebels when religious education has book of bible

parts.note: RE is the school subject religious education
Acts is a New Testament book

explanation.surface: Rebellion follows when scripture lessons cover a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebels' is a verb here: it means responds, and RE is the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel against something is to respond to it in opposition, a loose verb sense.

clue.text: Liberated female about to take drug

parts.note: re means about, concerning
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A freed woman is on the verge of taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to take' reads like 'just going to take', but 'about' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means released or at liberty.

clue.text: About to meet vehicle in country lane? One pulls back

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a tractor is a farm vehicle met on country lanes

explanation.surface: Meeting a farm vehicle on a narrow lane forces someone to back up.
explanation.walkthrough: A retractor is a surgical instrument that holds back the edges of a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical retractor draws tissue aside, an instrument that withdraws.

clue.text: A ship said to be resting in the water

indicators.note: said means the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: a tanker is a ship, so a ship is a tanker

explanation.surface: A ship is reported to be lying idle in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives the sound of A TANKER, which is spelt AT ANCHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel moored by its heavy hook stays still, floating without moving.

clue.text: Goat gets crop on south of the island

indicators.note: on south of means in this down entry the crop word sits below the island

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A goat feeds on a crop grown in the south of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on south of' places CORN below CAPRI in the down entry. Capricorn is the zodiac sign of the goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the tenth sign of the zodiac, is symbolised by a sea-goat.

clue.text: Most angry if tree is destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of these words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone is furious because a tree has been felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges IF TREE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiery means hot-tempered, so the superlative is the most hot-tempered.

clue.text: A threesome trashing one big town in appalling act

indicators.note: trashing means wrecking part of the group word by throwing out a letter

parts.note: a trio is a threesome
I is the Roman numeral one
a city is a big town

explanation.surface: A trio trashing a big town commits an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashing one' removes the I from TRIO, leaving TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a shockingly cruel or wicked deed.

clue.text: Someone who's been given an honour, look!

definitions.text: Someone who's been given an honour

explanation.surface: Someone honoured is told to take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble given a title such as baron is a lord; to stare closely is to gaze or squint.

clue.text: Went off course — not right, you should have waited!

indicators.note: not means the right letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to stray is to go off course

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off route and is told they should have waited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' takes R out of STRAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or wait where one is.

clue.text: Agent returning to river in van

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: returning means the agent word comes back, read the other way

parts.note: a rep, representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: An agent drives back to the river in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reads REP backwards, joined to CAM. A camper van is a motor home.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor caravan for holidaymakers is a camper.

clue.text: Accident puts Rex in pain

indicators.note: in means the king's letter is put within the pain word

parts.note: a pang is a sharp pain
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A crash leaves Rex in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, especially a minor car accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a minor crash or collision.

clue.text: Plans to have school punishment dismissed originally

indicators.note: originally means the dismissed word comes first, before the other

parts.note: a batter dismissed in cricket is out
lines are a school punishment of writing a sentence many times

explanation.surface: Plans are made to have a traditional school punishment scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' puts OUT at the start. Lines are a British school punishment: copying a sentence out many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough sketches or summaries of a scheme are drafts of what is intended.

clue.text: Bird landing finally in tree after flying

indicators.note: in means the final letter sits within the jumbled tree
flying suggests something scattered, so the letters of tree are rearranged
finally means only the last letter of landing is used

explanation.surface: A bird lands in a tree after flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' turns TREE into ERET, 'finally' takes G from landing, and 'in' puts it after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white wading heron.

clue.text: Some hit — magnificent old show!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A celebrated old programme was a magnificent hit.
explanation.walkthrough: ITMA (It's That Man Again) was a hugely popular BBC radio comedy of the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: It's That Man Again was a wartime BBC radio comedy programme.

clue.text: When disturbed, dreamy bore becomes abrasive

indicators.note: when disturbed means the letters of these two words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A dreamy bore turns harsh when disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When disturbed' rearranges DREAMY BORE. 'Abrasive' is a noun here: something that rubs down.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file coated with emery grit is a rough rubbing tool.

clue.text: Cheer up when a holiday resort is mentioned

indicators.note: is mentioned means the resort's name is spoken out loud

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on the English south coast

explanation.surface: Spirits lift whenever a seaside town comes up in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON, a seaside resort south of London, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten someone's mood or become more cheerful is to lift spirits.

clue.text: Give time for number to get back in

indicators.note: in means the number word is placed inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: to get back means the number abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone offers a time for a number to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' turns the abbreviation round to make ON, and 'in' is the container signal; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give as a gift, especially to charity.
